variants.title: Launch-day spike
variants.context: A product launches with 4,000 req/s and one app server reaches 96% CPU in 90 seconds.
variants.constraint: Requests queue and the same server handles all work.
variants.question: What is the first fix you choose?
variants.expectedPattern: Run several identical stateless app servers and spread traffic across them.

variants.title: Nightly import burst
variants.context: A nightly job sends 12,000 API requests in 30 seconds and one server sits saturated.
variants.constraint: The services are stateful on a single node.
variants.question: What architectural pattern reduces the failure risk most cleanly?
variants.expectedPattern: Scale horizontally with stateless workers behind a shared entry point.

variants.title: Microservice rollout
variants.context: A new microservice is deployed and traffic to it jumps from 500 to 15,000 req/s.
variants.constraint: Only one service instance exists and it hits CPU limits.
variants.question: What should happen next?
variants.expectedPattern: Add more identical instances and route work across them.
wrongChoices: Move traffic to a single backup node
Keep all traffic on one host

variants.title: Background worker backlog
variants.context: A background worker is doing image processing and the queue is growing faster than it drains.
variants.constraint: One worker is overloaded while others are idle.
variants.question: Which operating model restores capacity?
variants.expectedPattern: Run multiple workers that all pull from the same work queue.
wrongChoices: Add more retries on the same task

variants.title: API traffic from one region
variants.context: An API in one region grows from 1k to 20k req/s, but all users hit the same app instance.
variants.constraint: The rest of the fleet does almost no work.
variants.question: What is the fundamental mismatch?
variants.expectedPattern: Traffic is not evenly distributed, so the fleet is underutilized.

variants.title: One crash takes the whole service down
variants.context: The app service keeps user session state in memory and loses all sessions when the process dies.
variants.constraint: The system is not stateless and cannot be rebuilt quickly.
variants.question: What is the design issue behind the outage?
variants.expectedPattern: Sessions and app state must be externalized or removed from process-local memory.

variants.title: Hot service with no redundancy
variants.context: One search service handles every request while other instances are maintained but unused.
variants.constraint: The entry path still targets a single endpoint.
variants.question: How do you improve resilience?
variants.expectedPattern: Distribute requests to a fleet and remove single-host routing.
wrongChoices: Add a bigger CPU on the same node

variants.title: Tricky burst from social traffic
variants.context: A product’s traffic spikes after a social media mention, but the app server pool is small and homogeneous.
variants.constraint: No instance is stateful and one instance can no longer keep up.
variants.question: What changes the system from fragile to resilient?
variants.expectedPattern: Add more stateless instances behind a shared entry route.

variants.title: Long-running job fan-out
variants.context: A service watches for new files and processes them one at a time, so latency grows with each upload.
variants.constraint: Work is serial and CPU-bound on a single instance.
variants.question: What is the cleanest fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Parallelize work across multiple stateless workers.
wrongChoices: Move to a single giant machine

variants.title: Election-day traffic surge
variants.context: Users hit a public API as a live event starts, and one app instance exceeds 100% CPU.
variants.constraint: The event is short but intense; capacity must be elastic.
variants.question: How do you prepare for this kind of event?
variants.expectedPattern: Add multiple stateless app instances in advance and route traffic to them.

variants.title: Chat gateway saturates at peak hour
variants.context: A realtime chat gateway holds 80,000 sockets on one process and CPU climbs past 90% every evening.
variants.constraint: Connection state lives in that process, so extra machines cannot accept sockets yet.
variants.question: What must change before you can add capacity?
variants.expectedPattern: Externalize connection or session state so more identical gateways can share the load.
wrongChoices: Move chat history into the same process

variants.title: PDF renderer becomes the bottleneck
variants.context: Invoice PDFs are rendered in the web process and p95 latency jumps from 200ms to 8s during month-end.
variants.constraint: Rendering is CPU-heavy and does not need to finish inside the HTTP request.
variants.question: How do you restore headroom on the web tier?
variants.expectedPattern: Move rendering onto a pool of identical workers that can grow independently of the web servers.

variants.title: Autoscaler never fires
variants.context: CPU on the only app VM sits at 85% for 20 minutes, but no extra capacity appears.
variants.constraint: The service is a single instance with no replica set defined.
variants.question: Why does elasticity fail?
variants.expectedPattern: Horizontal scaling needs more than one replica target; a single node cannot autoscale out.

variants.title: Black Friday checkout farm
variants.context: Checkout traffic is 12x normal, and a pair of app servers both sit above 95% CPU.
variants.constraint: The app is already stateless and sessions live in Redis.
variants.question: What is the next capacity move?
variants.expectedPattern: Add more identical checkout instances and let the entry layer spread requests.
wrongChoices: Double the timeout on payment calls
Pin all carts to one server

variants.title: ML inference on a single GPU box
variants.context: A recommendation API runs inference on one GPU host and queue wait time grows during a campaign.
variants.constraint: Models are stateless at request time and can run on any replica.
variants.question: How do you absorb the extra inference load?
variants.expectedPattern: Run multiple identical inference replicas and distribute requests across them.
wrongChoices: Batch every request into one giant GPU job on the same box
Move inference into the primary database

variants.title: WebSocket fan-out on one node
variants.context: A live sports score service pushes updates from one node to every connected client.
variants.constraint: A node crash drops every live connection.
variants.question: What design removes the single-node blast radius?
variants.expectedPattern: Run several stateless fan-out nodes and share pub/sub so any node can serve clients.
wrongChoices: Keep all sockets on the fastest machine
Store live scores only in process memory
Increase TCP backlog on that one node

variants.title: Cron job on the app server
variants.context: A daily report job runs inside the only app process and saturates CPU for 40 minutes.
variants.constraint: User traffic shares that process and p99 latency explodes during the job.
variants.question: How do you protect interactive traffic?
variants.expectedPattern: Move the job to a separately scaled worker fleet so web instances stay dedicated to requests.
wrongChoices: Run the cron more often on the same process
Increase the web timeout to 40 minutes
Disable health checks during the job

variants.title: Sticky sessions block scale-out
variants.context: You add four app servers, but most users still land on the original node.
variants.constraint: Session affinity is based on in-memory session IDs.
variants.question: What unblocks true horizontal scale?
variants.expectedPattern: Store sessions outside the process so any instance can serve any user.

variants.title: Search indexer cannot keep up
variants.context: Document ingest is 3x faster than a single indexer can write into the search cluster.
variants.constraint: Indexing work is independent per document.
variants.question: What operating change restores ingest rate?
variants.expectedPattern: Run multiple identical indexers consuming the same ingest queue.
wrongChoices: Index only on the web request path
Increase search replica count without more indexers

variants.title: Regional failover needs spare capacity
variants.context: Primary region dies and the secondary has only one app instance, which immediately overloads.
variants.constraint: Failover traffic is the full production load.
variants.question: What should have been in place?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep multiple scaled-out instances in the failover region, not a single warm box.
wrongChoices: A bigger disk in the secondary region
A single oversized VM as the only standby
